subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which nutrient is most important for the growth and repair of muscle tissue?
questions.explain: Proteins provide amino acids needed for the growth and repair of body tissues including muscle.

questions.q: Fats are an important nutrient because they:
options: Cannot be stored by the body
Provide a slow-release energy source and insulation
questions.explain: Fats provide a concentrated, slow-release energy store and help insulate the body.

questions.q: Why is hydration important for a performer?
options: It removes the need for carbohydrates
It prevents a drop in performance and helps regulate body temperature
questions.explain: Staying hydrated maintains blood volume and temperature control, preventing dehydration and a fall in performance.

questions.q: Using the formula 220 - age, what is the maximum heart rate of a 16-year-old?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 16 = 204 bpm.

questions.q: Which somatotype is muscular and broad-shouldered, often suited to power sports?
questions.explain: Mesomorphs are muscular, broad-shouldered and well suited to strength and power events.

questions.q: The multi-stage fitness test (bleep test) measures which component of fitness?
questions.explain: The bleep test estimates aerobic capacity, a measure of cardiovascular endurance.

questions.q: Which of these is a benefit of regular physical activity for physical health?
options: Reduced risk of coronary heart disease
questions.explain: Regular exercise strengthens the heart and reduces the risk of coronary heart disease.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a cool-down after exercise?
options: To gradually lower heart rate and remove waste products
questions.explain: A cool-down gradually lowers heart rate and helps remove lactic acid, reducing stiffness.

Having a large amount of muscle
questions.explain: Obesity is an excessive accumulation of body fat that may negatively affect health.

questions.q: The sit-and-reach test is used to measure:
questions.explain: The sit-and-reach test measures flexibility, particularly of the lower back and hamstrings.

questions.q: Which method involves periods of work followed by periods of rest or recovery?
questions.explain: Interval training alternates bouts of work with rest periods.

questions.q: Mixing with others and making friends through sport is an example of which type of well-being?
questions.explain: Social well-being involves interacting with others, cooperating and forming friendships.
